title: kith-peer: DeliverHandler validate and store incoming attachment metadata
description:
What: Extend DeliverHandler in kith-peer to validate peer-supplied attachment metadata and insert rows into the attachments table.

Algorithm:
1. Add optional attachments: Option<Vec<Value>> to PeerDeliverArgs / InboundMessage deserialization.
2. After step 7 (ULID validation) and before DB write, validate each attachment:
   a. validate_blob_id(&blob_id) — reject path traversal.
   b. filename: reject ../, /, \, \0, len > 255.
   c. contentType: must contain /; reject newlines; len <= 256.
   d. size: must be u64 <= 104_857_600.
   e. sha256: must be 64 lowercase hex chars.
   f. Limit: max 20 attachments. Reject if exceeded.
3. All validation MUST occur BEFORE message insert.
4. After message insert, insert each attachment row: store.attachments().insert(&blob_id, &msg_id, &filename, &content_type, size, &sha256, now_unix).
5. Wrap message insert + attachment inserts in unchecked_transaction.
6. On any attachment validation failure: return invalidArguments, no DB write.

Defensive rules: all validation before any write; peer-supplied sha256/size/filename/contentType are all untrusted; reject partial inserts by using transaction; validate_blob_id before file system use; blobId from peer is stored as metadata only — actual blob bytes are fetched lazily (Phase 2 design).

Agent team: R reads DeliverHandler validation flow and existing transaction patterns; I implements; T writes tests: deliver with valid attachment metadata succeeds, malicious filename rejected with no DB write (zero-write assertion), oversized attachment rejected, max count exceeded rejected; V runs cargo test -p kith-peer + clippy.
